title: The arrow of time in quantum measurement
bottleneck: The Schrödinger equation is time-reversible, yet measurement appears irreversible: once an outcome is recorded it cannot be un-recorded, and entropy increases. No agreed account derives this irreversibility from the reversible dynamics without importing it through assumptions about initial conditions or the observer.
why_it_blocks: The tension between reversible microphysics and irreversible observation sits at the junction of quantum foundations and statistical mechanics; solving one side alone leaves the other mysterious.
current_state: Most physicists attribute the arrow to the universe's low-entropy initial state plus decoherence, but why the initial state had such low entropy, the Past Hypothesis, is itself unexplained. Boltzmann's statistical account traces irreversibility to the low-entropy Past Hypothesis, which itself remains the deepest unexplained initial condition in all of known physics, dwarfing even the cosmological constant problem in severity.
